newsitem.title: PUERTO RICO: Toll in Puerto Rico blast reaches 29.
newsitem.headline: Toll in Puerto Rico blast reaches 29.

text.p: The confirmed death toll from an explosion that gutted a San Juan commercial building climbed to 29 Tuesday as lawyers for the victims' families demanded access to the blast site.

Rescue workers pulled the 29th body -- that of a woman -- from the rubble of the Humberto Vidal office building in the Puerto Rican capital's Rio Piedras district, police said. In addition to the 29 dead, seven people were missing and 12 remained in hospitals, police said. About 70 people were hurt.

Authories believe the explosion last Thursday was caused by a natural gas leak. But investigators were analysing what was described as a "combustible substance" found near the site, which police spokeswoman Marilyn Calo said they believed to be gasoline. "But they haven't said anything officially yet," she said.
Several cars were destroyed in the blast, which ripped through the six-story building and showered debris onto a school and shops several hundred yards away.

"Our people are still doing testing. They're testing the ground around the building, looking for combustibles," Paul Schlamm of the National Transportation Safety Board in Washington told Reuters. "They've reached no conclusion."

Lawyers representing the victims and their families have hired chemical explosives experts and are asking the U.S. district court to grant them access to the blast site. Police barred the attorneys from inspecting the site and a federal judge refused to hear a motion they filed on Monday.

Attorneys Jorge Ortiz and Francisco Troncoso say they must collect crucial evidence to bolster their legal claim. They allege that San Juan Gas Co., a subsidiary of Houston-based Enron Corp., was negligent in not maintaining the gas lines that run under the city.
San Juan gas workers were probing a complaint about a strong gas odour when the explosion occured.

Troncoso said he would file a $10 million federal law suit against Enron for alleged negligence in the death of Wilma Valle, 29. On Friday he filed a $6 million claim against Enron on behalf of a woman who suffered a broken arm, broken ribs, a perforated lung and a broken left knee in the explosion.
A mass for victims conducted by Cardinal Luis Aponte Martinez of San Juan is scheduled for Wednesday night.
